question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution instructs the State to ensure the right to work, education and public assistance in specific circumstances?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 41**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 41** of the Constitution of India falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV of the Constitution).
 
• It specifically instructs the State to make provisions for securing the **right to work, education, and public assistance** in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement, and in other cases of undeserved want.
 
• Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court but are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• **Article 41** emphasizes the responsibility of the State to ensure social and economic justice to its citizens.
 
• The provisions under Article 41 aim to reduce inequalities and promote welfare measures for disadvantaged sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• DPSPs are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution under Articles 36 to 51.
 
• They are inspired by the **Irish Constitution** and are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts.
 
• The objective of DPSPs is to establish social and economic democracy and welfare in the country.
 
 
 
• **Article 38:**
 
 
• It directs the State to strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order in which **justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all institutions**.
 
 
 
• **Article 45:**
 
 
• Originally, Article 45 aimed to provide free and compulsory education for children up to the age of 14 years within ten years of the Constitution's adoption.
 
• It was later amended by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002**, which made elementary education a fundamental right under Article 21A.
 
 
 
• **Article 48:**
 
 
• It directs the State to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and to preserve and improve breeds and prohibit the slaughter of cows and calves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Directive Principles** act as guidelines for the government to frame laws and policies aimed at achieving socio-economic justice.
 
• Although not enforceable, they are fundamental for governance and the State is expected to apply them in its administration.
 
• The courts have upheld the importance of DPSPs in various judgments, stating that they are as significant as Fundamental Rights in guiding government policies.
 
• While **Article 41** specifically deals with the right to work, education, and public assistance, other articles like **39, 42, 43** complement it by addressing related issues like health, equal pay, and living wages.
